items.excerpt: Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can reach the heights achieved under Sir Alex Ferguson but is not expecting the same level of patience.
body: Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can reach the heights achieved under Sir Alex Ferguson but is not expecting the same level of patience.

Friday marks 40 years since Ferguson was appointed United manager on November 6, 1986. It is an anniversary that comes at a particularly significant moment for the club, with Carrick's position in charge still facing intense scrutiny.

United's dramatic 3-2 comeback victory over Roma in midweek offered Carrick some much-needed breathing space after a nine-game winless run, but Sunday's Premier League clash against Aston Villa, live on Sky, represents another significant test. items.title: Jobe joins brother Jude with England to showcase his own talent
items.excerpt: "He's coming on his own merit," said Thomas Tuchel, after extolling the strengths of Jobe Bellingham.
body: "He's coming on his own merit," said Thomas Tuchel, after extolling the strengths of Jobe Bellingham.

Jude Bellingham's younger brother - as is currently the go-to preface to any description of Jobe - couldn't hide his delight when he got the call from Tuchel to say he was being promoted from U21s captain to be included in the England senior squad.

"It's an incredible achievement for the family, for both brothers to be called up by their national team," Tuchel said on Friday, after revealing his squad for the Nations League games with Croatia and Spain. "I saw his excitement straightaway in his smile."

But Tuchel was also right to highlight the individual qualities of 21-year-old Jobe and the different attributes he can offer the national team, in a different position to his brother. items.title: 'It's not personal' - Tuchel explains Palmer exclusion
items.excerpt: Thomas Tuchel has insisted Cole Palmer's absence from the England squad isn't "personal" - but sent out an emphatic statement with the Chelsea star's exclusion.
body: Thomas Tuchel has insisted Cole Palmer's absence from the England squad isn't "personal" - but sent out an emphatic statement with the Chelsea star's exclusion.

Palmer is in form and a check from the England medical staff with Chelsea confirmed he is fit and ready to play this weekend. But Tuchel has prioritised players who were available and delivered in the previous international break.
Tuchel made headlines in September when he said Palmer misses too many opportunities to impress him, following the attacker's withdrawal due to injury.

During Tuchel's tenure Palmer has been unavailable for selection because of injury three times and has withdrawn from a further two squads. For the November Nations League games with Croatia and Spain , the England boss is putting his trust in the players who have shown him up close what they can do. items.excerpt: Everton are seventh in the Premier League table with the chance to move above Liverpool into fifth if they can beat Coventry at home. They are also into a Carabao Cup quarter-final against Fleetwood. This has been a promising start for Davi…
body: Everton are seventh in the Premier League table with the chance to move above Liverpool into fifth if they can beat Coventry at home. They are also into a Carabao Cup quarter-final against Fleetwood. This has been a promising start for David Moyes.

"When you start to talk about quarter-finals, it sounds good," Moyes tells Sky Sports . "Every Evertonian wants a cup run because we have been so long since we have been near lifting any trophies. My expectations are that I want us to be challenging."

There was not huge optimism at the start of the season when Everton sold Iliman Ndiaye and were unable to make the signings they had hoped for late in the transfer window. items.title: 'I could have carried on' - Coady announces retirement at 33
items.excerpt: Conor Coady has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 33.
body: Conor Coady has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 33.
Speaking on Sky Sports News, Coady said: "I'm really proud to have played this unbelievable game for so long. I think I'm ready and there.
"The last couple of years have been tough, I've been obsessed with playing football for so long that when I haven't, it's hard. But I'm super, super proud with how the last 15 year have gone.

"Physically I'm absolutely fine, I feel good and I feel strong. I could have carried on playing, but I want to look forward to the next bit. I could have carried on playing and sat on the bench, but I've been sat on the bench for the last couple of years and I've found it tough. It happens and comes to everyone."

body: Depleted Hearts' Conference League bruising was almost totally self-inflicted in a 3-1 defeat by Thun in Switzerland.

Belgian boss Wouter Vrancken was without 10 players through various ailments and the Scottish team were dealt another blow in the 22nd minute when defender Jamie McCart put through his own goal in calamitous fashion.

items.title: Pressure ramps up on Le Bris as Sunderland beaten by Dinamo Zagreb
items.excerpt: Pressure is ramping up even more on Regis Le Bris as Sunderland were comfortably beaten 2-0 by Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League to continue the Black Cats' torrid run of form.
body: Pressure is ramping up even more on Regis Le Bris as Sunderland were comfortably beaten 2-0 by Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League to continue the Black Cats' torrid run of form.
Before the game, Le Bris said Sunderland have been too exposed and leaky in defence - but his team were not listening as they went in 2-0 down at half-time in front of an angry Stadium of Light.

Poor marking from a corner allowed Luka Stojkovic to volley in the first goal - then the Dinamo midfielder set up Dion Beljo with a delightful chipped pass, with his deft finish equally sweet, although the red and white defenders were all at sea in the move.

At the other end of the pitch, Sunderland were a little more unfortunate. They struck the woodwork in both halves through defenders Thomas Meunier and Kevin Danso. Heroic defending from Dinamo also denied Malick Fofana and Trai Hume in the same move with last-ditch blocks.
